newsitem.title: FRANCE: Virgin, French group join Air Liberte race -papers.
newsitem.headline: Virgin, French group join Air Liberte race -papers.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express and a consortium led by French travel company Nouvelles Frontieres have bid for French airline Air Liberte, French newspapers reported on Tuesday.
Added to an offer unveiled by British Airways on Monday, at least three candidates are now lining up to run the insolvent airline with its precious landing slots, they said.
Les Echos business daily said there were signs that Fernand Danan, a pilot board member of AOM airlines, had also gathered a consortium in time for Monday's deadline for bids.
Only the British Airways bid has been officially confirmed.
Virgin, French group join Air Liberte =2
None of the companies involved in the other two reported bids were immediately available for comment.
But Morocco's state airline Royal Air Maroc (RAM) announced overnight that it was involved in a bid with a French group to purchase Air Liberte.
It said its bid was associated with Financiere Moncey, a subsidiary of the Groupe Rivaud bank. The Moroccan airline said it would participate at a level of 10 to 15 percent.
Paris financial daily La Tribune Desfosses said Groupe Rivaud was involved in the bid drawn up by Nouvelles Frontieres.
It called the bid an unexpectedly complex manoeuvre designed to meet the government's objectives for a "French solution" to the problems of the ailing private French airline fleet.
British Airways submitted its 25 million franc bid on Monday in spite of reports France would resist a foreign bidder,
La Tribune quoted Nouvelles Frontieres chairman Jacques Maillot as saying he planned to continue running Air Liberte as a business rather than to absorb it through merger.
Les Echos said Groupe Rivaud, the leading shareholder in Air Liberte until the airline went into administration in September, would keep 75 to 80 percent of the airline under the same plan.
British Airways said on Monday it thought it could revive Air Liberte by merging it with its own French subsidiary TAT.
But Le Monde reported on the same day that Prime Minister Alain Juppe was pressing for a French bid for Air Liberte to establish a domestic competitor to state-owned Air France.
Air Liberte owns around a quarter of the slots at Orly, Paris' second airport. It lost 650 million francs in the fiirst nine months of 1996 and has 1.5 billion francs of debt.
